s: India won the men's Asian Champions Trophy hockey 2026 at Mohali by defeating which team in the final?
x: India beat Japan 4-1 in the final at Mohali on 5 Nov 2026; Malaysia took bronze.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 2026 Asian Champions Trophy was India's record sixth title in the event.
2. It completed a hat-trick of consecutive titles for India.
3. India lost one league match but won the final.
Which of the above is/are correct?
x: India won its 6th title and a third straight one, finishing unbeaten with seven wins in seven matches, so statement 3 is wrong.

s: The final of the men's Asian Champions Trophy hockey 2026 was played at which venue?
o: Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium, New Delhi
Olympian Balbir Singh Senior International Hockey Stadium, Mohali
x: The 2026 final (India 4-1 Japan) was at the Olympian Balbir Singh Senior International Hockey Stadium, Mohali, Punjab.

s: Who became the first Indian woman to reach the badminton semi-finals at the Youth Olympic Games (Dakar 2026)?
x: Tanvi Patri (15, Odisha) reached the Dakar 2026 YOG semi-finals and went on to win silver.

s: Khushbu Rajakbhai Darjada, the first medallist from the Siddi community at the Youth Olympic Games (Dakar 2026), won silver in which sport?
x: She won silver in girls' 63 kg judo at Dakar 2026.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Siddis are a community of African origin.
2. Siddis were recognised as a Scheduled Tribe in parts of Gujarat in 1956.
3. Siddis live only in Gujarat.
Which of the above is/are correct?
x: Siddis are of East African origin and an ST in parts of Gujarat since 1956, but they also live in Karnataka, Maharashtra, Goa and Daman and Diu.

s:
Match the Indian athlete with the sport of the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympics medal:
A. Taniya   B. Dhinidhi Desinghu   C. Rajkumari Lanchenbi Chanu   D. Tirthank Pegu
1. Wushu   2. Beach wrestling   3. Swimming (butterfly)   4. Swimming (freestyle)
x: Taniya - 75 kg beach wrestling silver; Dhinidhi - 100 m and 200 m freestyle bronzes; Lanchenbi Chanu - wushu bronze; Tirthank Pegu - 200 m butterfly bronze.

s: Who became India's 100th chess Grandmaster in November 2026?
x: Anuj Shrivatri of Katni (MP) became India's 100th GM on 8 Nov 2026; Rathanvel was the 99th.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Anuj Shrivatri earned the GM title by winning the 7th ASEAN Plus Individual Open Chess Championship in the Philippines.
2. He is the first Grandmaster from Madhya Pradesh.
3. V.S. Rathanvel became India's 99th Grandmaster in July 2026.
Which of the above is/are correct?
x: All three: Shrivatri won the event at Ozamiz City (Philippines), is MP's first GM, and Rathanvel was the 99th GM in July 2026.

s: At the ISSF World Championship 2026 in Doha, India won the gold medal in which team event?
x: Esha Singh, Manu Bhaker and Divya Thadigol Subbaraju won the women's 25 m pistol team gold; the men's 50 m 3P team won bronze.

s: Who won the women's singles title at the Korea Open 2026 badminton tournament?
x: South Korea's An Se-young beat Japan's Akane Yamaguchi in the final on 8 Nov 2026.

s: The Hylo Open badminton tournament, won by P.V. Sindhu and Lakshya Sen in 2026, was earlier known as the:
x: The Hylo Open at Saarbrücken (held since 1988) was formerly the BMW Badminton Cup.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football in November 2026.
2. He made his debut for Portugal in 2003.
3. He never won a major international trophy with Portugal.
Which of the above is/are correct?
x: Ronaldo retired on 5 Nov 2026 after a debut in 2003; he won Euro 2016 and the Nations League (2019, 2025), so statement 3 is wrong.

s: With how many international goals did Cristiano Ronaldo end his Portugal career in November 2026?
x: Ronaldo retired with 146 goals in 234 caps, both records.

s: Valasanaini Ravanni, who won two bronze medals at the 5th Asian Para Games 2026, belongs to which district of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Ravanni, a visually impaired athlete from near Paderu, Alluri Sitharama Raju district, won bronzes in the 400 m and 1,500 m.

s:
Match the Andhra Pradesh para-athlete with the 2026 Asian Para Games achievement:
A. Ravi Karthik Budigina   B. Ravi Rongali   C. Valasanaini Ravanni
1. Bronze in shot put   2. Silver in 100 m freestyle swimming   3. Bronzes in 400 m and 1,500 m
x: Budigina (Eluru) won silver in 100 m freestyle, India's first swimming medal at the Games; Rongali (Anakapalli) bronze in shot put; Ravanni two bronzes in 400 m and 1,500 m.

s: How many medals did India win at the 5th Asian Para Games 2026 (Aichi-Nagoya)?
x: 97 Indian para-athletes won 114 medals (30 G, 35 S, 49 B); the PM felicitated them on 7 Nov 2026.

s: The inaugural Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship 2026, in which India won both titles, was held in:
x: It was held in Ahmedabad with 13 men's and 10 women's teams.

s: At the All India Sainik Schools National Games 2026, held at Bijapur, which Sainik School won the junior boys' volleyball title?
x: Sainik School Amaravatinagar won junior boys' volleyball; Ghorakhal won junior boys' basketball.

s: National Education Day, observed on 11 November, marks the birth anniversary of:
x: 11 Nov is Maulana Azad's birth anniversary (b. 1888); Radhakrishnan's birthday (5 Sept) is Teachers' Day.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was born in Mecca.
2. He started the Urdu weekly Al-Hilal in 1912.
3. He presided over the Ramgarh session of the INC in 1940.
Which of the above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: born 11 Nov 1888 in Mecca, Al-Hilal 1912, INC President from Ramgarh 1940 to 1946.

s: What is the theme of World Diabetes Day 2026 (14 November)?
o: Know your risk, know your response
x: IDF/WHO: 'Early action on diabetes', a two-year theme for 2026-27.

s: World Diabetes Day is observed on 14 November because it is the birth anniversary of:
x: 14 Nov is the birthday of Sir Frederick Banting, who co-discovered insulin with Charles Best in 1921.

s: What was the theme of World Tsunami Awareness Day 2026 (5 November)?
o: Be Tsunami Ready: Invest in Tsunami Preparedness
Be Tsunami Ready: Resilience Starts With You
Fighting Inequality for a Resilient Future
x: The 2026 slogan was 'Be Tsunami Ready: Resilience Starts With You'; 'Invest in Tsunami Preparedness' was the 2025 slogan.

s: The theme of World Science Day for Peace and Development 2026 (10 November) was:
x: UNESCO's 2026 theme: 'Common ground through science diplomacy'.

s: National Legal Services Day is observed on 9 November because on that date in 1995:
o: The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 came into force
Article 39A was inserted in the Constitution
The first Lok Adalat was held
x: The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 came into force on 9 Nov 1995; Article 39A dates from the 42nd Amendment (1976).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. NALSA is a statutory body under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
2. The Chief Justice of India is its Patron-in-Chief.
3. Free legal aid is a Directive Principle under Article 39A.
Which of the above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct; the Executive Chairman is a serving or retired SC judge.

s: National Entrepreneurship Day (9 November) marks the setting up, in 2014, of the:
o: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
x: The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship was set up on 9 Nov 2014; Startup India came in 2016.

s:
Arrange the following events related to 'Vande Mataram' in chronological order:
1. First published in the journal Bangadarshan
2. Included in the novel Anandamath
3. Sung by Tagore at the Calcutta session of the INC
4. Adopted as the National Song
x: Bangadarshan 7 Nov 1875, Anandamath 1882, INC session 1896, National Song 24 Jan 1950.

s: The 150th anniversary of 'Vande Mataram' marked in November 2026 counts from its first publication in which journal on 7 November 1875?
x: Vande Mataram first appeared in Bangadarshan on 7 Nov 1875; the Railways ended their year-long celebration in Nov 2026.

s: Which one of the following States did NOT come into being (in its present or earlier form) on 1 November 1956?
x: Haryana was carved out of Punjab on 1 Nov 1966; AP, Kerala, MP, Mysore and Madras date from 1 Nov 1956.

s: Who won the Booker Prize 2026?
x: M. John Harrison won on 9 Nov 2026 for 'The End of Everything'; Szalay won in 2025, and Yáng won the International Booker 2026.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. M. John Harrison won the Booker Prize 2026 for 'The End of Everything'.
2. At 81, he is the oldest winner of the Booker Prize.
3. The International Booker Prize 2026 was won by 'Heart Lamp'.
Which of the above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; 'Heart Lamp' (Banu Mushtaq) won the International Booker in 2025, and the 2026 winner was 'Taiwan Travelogue'.

s: 'Belonging: A Journey of Love', released on 10 November 2026, is the memoir of:
x: Sonia Gandhi's memoir was published by HarperCollins India on 10 Nov 2026.

s: Nirmala Lakshman won the Sharjah Award for Best International Non-Fiction Book (2026) for which book?
o: The Tamils: A Portrait of a Community
x: 'The Tamils: A Portrait of a Community' by Nirmala Lakshman, Director of The Hindu Group.

s:
Match the manuscript added to UNESCO's Memory of the World Asia-Pacific Register (2026) with its author:
A. Rajatarangini   B. Arthashastra   C. Panchatantra   D. Ramcharitmanas
1. Kautilya   2. Kalhana   3. Tulsidas   4. Vishnu Sharma
x: Rajatarangini - Kalhana; Arthashastra - Kautilya; Panchatantra - Vishnu Sharma; Ramcharitmanas - Tulsidas.

s: UNESCO's Memory of the World programme, to whose Asia-Pacific register the Mahabharata manuscripts were added in 2026, was launched in:
x: The Memory of the World programme for documentary heritage was launched in 1992.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. C.P. Brown published 'A Dictionary, Telugu and English' in 1852.
2. He collected and published the poems of Yogi Vemana.
3. The C.P. Brown Library is located in Visakhapatnam.
Which of the above is/are correct?
x: The C.P. Brown Library is in Kadapa (where Brown was Deputy Collector), not Visakhapatnam.

s: Who is popularly called the 'Father of Modern Telugu Literature' and the 'Restless Pandit', whose birth anniversary (10 November) was marked by the AP CM in 2026?
x: Charles Philip Brown (1798-1884), born 10 Nov 1798 in Calcutta.

s: Where will the 19th Pravasi Bharatiya Divas Convention be held in January 2027?
x: Kolkata, 7-9 Jan 2027; the 2025 (18th) convention was at Bhubaneswar.

s: Which Indian museum was ranked 1st in Asia and 9th in the world in the 'World's 100 Best Museums 2026' list?
o: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya, Mumbai
x: The Bihar Museum, Patna, designed by Fumihiko Maki, was ranked 1st in Asia and 9th globally by Worth a Journey.

s: Sanjit 'Bunker' Roy, who died on 10 November 2026, founded which institution?
x: Bunker Roy set up the SWRC at Tilonia, Rajasthan, in 1972, later known as Barefoot College; MKSS was co-founded by his wife Aruna Roy.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Barefoot College began as the Social Work and Research Centre in 1972.
2. Bunker Roy received the Padma Shri in 1986.
3. Barefoot College is located in Gujarat.
Which of the above is/are correct?
x: Barefoot College is at Tilonia, Rajasthan; statements 1 and 2 are correct.

s: Neurosurgeon Dr Ashok Kumar Mahapatra, who died in November 2026, was the founding Director of:
x: Mahapatra was founding Director of AIIMS Bhubaneswar and led the 2017 separation of the conjoined twins Jaga and Balia.

s: Which footballer retired from international football on 5 November 2026 after 234 caps?
x: Cristiano Ronaldo (Portugal) retired after 234 caps and 146 goals; Messi had retired from international football in Aug 2026.

s: Dr Devi Shetty was conferred which French honour in November 2026?
o: Chevalier de l'Ordre national du Mérite
Ordre des Arts et des Lettres
Chevalier of the Order of Academic Palms
x: He received the Chevalier de l'Ordre national du Mérite, France's second-highest national order, for Covid-era support to the French community.

s:
Assertion (A): The Ordre national du Mérite is France's second-highest national order.
Reason (R): It ranks below the Legion of Honour and was set up by Charles de Gaulle in 1963.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Founded on 3 Dec 1963 by de Gaulle, the order ranks just below the Legion of Honour, which is why it is second-highest.

s: Union Civil Aviation Minister K. Ram Mohan Naidu was named in November 2026 among the '38 by 38' Achievers of which university?
x: Purdue University's College of Engineering; the award, inspired by Neil Armstrong, was instituted in 2024. Naidu did his BSEE at Purdue in 2008.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Purdue's '38 by 38' award was instituted in 2024.
2. It is inspired by Neil Armstrong, a Purdue alumnus.
3. Ram Mohan Naidu represents Srikakulam in the Lok Sabha.
Which of the above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: instituted in 2024, inspired by Armstrong (on the Moon at 38), and Naidu is the Srikakulam MP.

s: Who is the Chairperson of the National Medical Commission (as of November 2026)?
x: Dr Abhijat Chandrakant Sheth chairs the NMC, a body under the NMC Act 2019 set up in 2020.

s: Under Section 4(1) of the NMC Act, 2019, the National Medical Commission consists of how many members?
x: It has 33 members: a Chairperson, 10 ex officio members and 22 part-time members.

s: After Israel's new Knesset was sworn in on 10 November 2026, who was first given the chance to form a government?
x: Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, a former IDF chief, got the first chance; Netanyahu remains caretaker PM.

s: Anuj Shrivatri, India's 100th chess Grandmaster, is the first Grandmaster from which State?
x: Anuj Shrivatri of Katni is Madhya Pradesh's first GM (8 Nov 2026).
